question: Why do shorter flights produce more emissions per kilometre than longer ones?
gold_answer: Because the landing/take-off cycle has a strong influence on emissions
supporting_text: Short-haul flights have higher emission factors due to strong influence of the landing/take off cycle on emissions
model_answer: Short‑haul flights emit more greenhouse‑gas per kilometre because the landing‑and‑take‑off (LTO) cycle contributes a large share of the fuel burned and emissions; this fixed‑cost is spread over a relatively short distance, raising the emission factor. Long‑haul flights dilute the LTO impact over many kilometres, so their per‑km emissions are lower. [ghg_scope3 p.85]
